plan.title: fix(architecture): cover content modules in codeStructure validation

narratives.Description: Framework-content currently matches root repo-dev docs while 24 of 34 globs are dead, so MAP under-reports content/ skills and coding. This slice re-homes globs onto Content Manifest content stems, repairs content-packs to content/packs JSON, and adds a per-glob unmatched check with advisory-then-enforce rollout. Bound contract is lean 5513286022, not the pass-1 issue-body ACs.
narratives.Overview:
## Parent

#4085

## What to build

Repair `plan.architecture.codeStructure` and its validation so the declared framework-content and content-pack modules cover the real `content/**` tree, and so a required nonempty module cannot silently match zero files.

## Why

The canonical project definition declares globs such as `coding/**/*.md`, `skills/**/*.md`, and `packs/**`, while those files live below `content/`. The extractor therefore under-reports central product content and finds no content-pack files even though structure validation is green.

## Evidence

- `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json:28-65,115-121`
- `packages/core/src/codebase/default-extractor.ts:668-689`
- Audit result: 87 framework-content matches versus 298 Markdown files under `content/`, and zero content-pack matches despite tracked pack files
- Design provenance: #1595

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The intended current guidance under `content/**` is included in the framework-content module.
- [ ] `content/packs/**` produces nonzero content-pack matches.
- [ ] Module ownership and purpose text matches the corrected boundaries.
- [ ] A required nonempty module that matches zero files fails validation unless it explicitly declares an `allowEmpty`-style exception.
- [ ] Diagnostics name the module and unmatched globs.
- [ ] Reviewed module counts are covered by focused tests.
- [ ] `task codebase:validate-structure` and MAP generation pass.
- [ ] `task check` passes.

## Type

AFK

## Blocked by

None — can start immediately.

### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-02T16:53:38Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

SHA: `16e995470c73c9449d6ee137162912db091e9de6`. Open critique of issue #4088 (body + Stop 1 write-back 5513091916). Re-ran glob expansion with the same `node:fs.globSync` + file filter the default extractor uses (`packages/core/src/codebase/default-extractor.ts` `globFiles`).

The recorded design cannot bind as written. Repairing `pathGlobs` and failing a module whose *union* of globs matches zero files does not stop the silent under-reporting this issue measured, and it does not name which trees `framework-content` owns.

## 1. Module-level emptiness is the wrong fail-closed grain

class: `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** On this SHA, `framework-content` matches 87 files and `content-packs` matches 0. `validateCodeStructure` (`packages/core/src/verify-source/code-structure-validate.ts`) never expands `pathGlobs`; it checks shape, repository-relative spelling, and *string-equal* glob assignment (`CS-GLOB-CONFLICT`). Tree existence is used today only for glossary URIs and projection banners. Per-glob expansion of the dogfood record:

- `framework-content`: 34 globs, 10 live, 24 match zero. The module is still nonempty.
- `content-packs`: 2 globs, both zero (`packs/**/*.md`, `packs/**/*.json`; no repo-root `packs/`).
- `ci-release-automation`: nonempty, but `.github/**/*.yaml` is already dead.

The 10 live `framework-content` globs are not a partial view of `content/`. They are 7 root files plus root `docs/**/*.md` (76), root `incidents/**/*.md` (1), and root `meta/**/*.md` (3). That sums to 87. `content/coding`, `content/skills`, `content/docs`, and `content/meta` contribute 0. A required-nonempty module check would fail only `content-packs` and would leave the 24 dead `framework-content` globs green.

`globFiles` is private to the extractor and swallows glob errors. `MAX_FILES_PER_MODULE` is 100; `fileCount` is the full match set, `files[]` is truncated. Schema `CodeStructureModule` (`content/vbrief/schemas/vbrief-core.schema.json`) has no `allowEmpty`; `additionalProperties` is true. Existing fixtures (`code-structure-validate.test.ts` `minimalRecord` with `pathGlobs: ["AGENTS.md"]` in an empty temp tree, plus `coverage-boost.test.ts` fictional globs) would fail a tree-walk nonempty rule unless they grow files or an exception.

**Failure mode.** An implementer prefixes enough globs that `framework-content` stays nonempty (it already is), rewrites `content-packs` to `content/packs/**` (6 JSON files), and ships. Dead globs and wrong-tree globs remain authorable. MAP still omits `content/skills` and `content/coding`. A later rename of a live glob can resurrect a zero-match module that `allowEmpty` then silences at module grain, which reopens the `content-packs` hole.

**Disposition.** Bind only if the fail-closed rule is per unmatched glob (diagnostics already asked to name unmatched globs), the exception is the same grain, and validation uses the extractor's expander (`globSync` + `SKIP_DIRS` from `NON_PRODUCT_DIRS` + `build`). Module-union emptiness is not a sufficient control. Do not store match counts in authored `codeStructure` (`CS-DERIVED-FACT` already bans `filecount` / `files`).

## 2. Dual-home trees are unnamed, so "cover content/**" does not pick a module boundary

class: `blocks-the-design`

**Evidence.** Several glob first-segments exist in both trees, and the unprefixed spelling hits the root copy:

| glob | root matches | `content/` matches |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/**/*.md` | 76 | 32 (`content/docs/`) |
| `incidents/**/*.md` | 1 (real incident) | 2 (README + template) |
| `meta/**/*.md` | 3 (`ideas.md`, `lessons.md`, `suggestions.md`) | 8 (SOUL, security, …) |

Root-relative names that live only under `content/` currently match 0: `QUICK-START.md`, `UPGRADING.md`, `commands.md`, `glossary.md`. A naive `content/` prefix of directory globs still leaves those four dead, still leaves `content/core/**/*.md` dead (`core/` exists in neither tree), and *drops* root `docs/` / `incidents/` / `meta/` unless those unprefixed globs are kept.

`content/**/*.md` via `globSync` is 275 files (walk of `content/**/*.md` including dotdirs is 298; the 23 extras are `content/.agents/skills/**/SKILL.md`, which default `globSync` does not see). `content/packs/**` is 6 JSON files and does not overlap `content/**/*.md`. Content top-level dirs with no glob first-segment: `ci-cd` (6 md), `doctor`, `vbrief` (schemas + 1 md), `secrets`, `.agents`.

The AC "intended current guidance under `content/**`" can be read as (a) umbrella `content/**/*.md`, (b) re-home only the listed directory globs, or (c) dual-home both trees. Those three MAP memberships differ. Purpose text ("Agent-consumed standards, strategies, skills, templates, and documentation") does not choose.

**Failure mode.** Two AC-green glob sets own different files. Root maintainer `docs/` can fall out of `framework-content` as a side effect of prefixing, or `content/docs/` can stay invisible because `docs/**/*.md` already matches 76 files. `content/.agents` copies can be included or excluded by expander `dot` behavior without the AC noticing.

**Disposition.** Name the owned trees before bind: which of root `docs/` / `incidents/` / `meta/`, `content/` deposit sources, and `content/.agents` copies belong to `framework-content`; how dual-home names are spelled; whether unlisted `content/` dirs are in or out. `pathOwnership[]` already exists for cases module globs cannot express; overlapping glob *strings* are not today's `CS-GLOB-CONFLICT`.

## 3. The 87-versus-298 figure is true and the causal story is wrong

class: `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** 87 and 298 both reproduce. They are not a coverage ratio on one tree. 87 is almost disjoint from `content/`: it is root docs plus a few root files. 298 is a walk that includes 23 dotdir SKILL copies `globSync("content/**/*.md")` does not return (275).

**Failure mode.** Tests that pin "framework-content ≥ 298" or "coverage 87→298" will either fail against the extractor or pass while still matching the wrong tree. Reviewers will treat 87 as "some content files already counted."

**Disposition.** State the defect as wrong-tree + dead globs + never-expanded validation. Any "reviewed module counts" tests must name the expander, including nodot and `SKIP_DIRS`, and must not treat 298 as the extractor's number.

## 4. The empty-match rule is a #1595 profile change, not only a dogfood glob edit

class: `sharpens-framing`

**Evidence.** `codebase:validate-structure` is on `FRAMEWORK_CHECK_GATES` and not on `CONSUMER_CHECK_GATES`, but `evaluateCodeStructure` is the same command consumers run. No `codeStructure` → exit 0 (`OK: no codeStructure metadata found`). `--strict` only promotes existing warnings (`CS-BOUNDEDNESS`, `CS-SINGLE-FILE-MODULE`); default `task codebase:validate-structure` does not pass `--strict`. Profile docs list shape and discipline checks, not glob expansion against the tree.

**Failure mode.** Default fail-closed emptiness breaks placeholder modules and the in-repo temp-tree tests cited above. Putting the same rule behind `--strict` leaves `task check` green, which is the current defect. An untyped `allowEmpty` key on the module object is schema-legal today and invisible to the validator until the validator reads it.

**Disposition.** Record that this is a profile-wide tree-dependent check, the default (error vs warning vs `--strict`), and that `allowEmpty` is typed and consumed. Keep authored metadata free of derived counts (NFR-4 / `CS-DERIVED-FACT`).

## 5. Truncation and pack overlap

class: `footnote`

Covering `content/**/*.md` (275) puts `framework-content` over `MAX_FILES_PER_MODULE` (100). `fileCount` stays honest; MAP `files[]` truncates. `typescript-engine` (2247) and `vbrief-metadata` (1503) already truncate. "Included in the module" is the count, not the listed files.

`content/packs` is JSON-only on this SHA. Nonzero content-pack matches do not require a markdown glob. Issue cite `default-extractor.ts:668-689` is `buildCodebaseMap`; expansion is `globFiles` at 182–210 and `curatedModules` at 264–321. GitHub labels on #4088 are empty; the Stop 1 comment carries `mechanism-shaped: true` in prose only.

## Injection / swarm

The new check walks the working tree and then gates MAP membership. That is shared tree state. `SKIP_DIRS` already excludes `.deft-scratch`, `swarm-worktrees`, `.claude`, `node_modules`, `dist`, and `build` in the extractor only. A validator that calls raw `globSync` without that set can count nested agent checkouts as module files, or can disagree with MAP. Authored globs are already `safeRelativePath`-constrained; this is not untrusted issue-thread input. Close stdin is irrelevant here. The control is one shared expander, not reviewer attention.

## Road not taken

I considered accepting module-union emptiness plus a glob prefix as enough, because `content-packs` is the only fully empty module and a per-glob lint would fail this repo today (24 dead globs). That is also the strongest rejected position: per-glob fail-closed is a bigger profile hammer, and `--strict` unmatched-glob warnings would reuse `CS-BOUNDEDNESS` promotion.

What flips it: this SHA already shows a nonempty module matching the wrong tree with 24 dead globs. Module-union emptiness cannot be the control that "stops silent under-reporting." `--strict` is opt-in and is not how `task check` invokes the validator, so a warning-only unmatched glob stays green.

I also considered an umbrella `content/**/*.md` instead of re-homing the listed globs. That includes `content/` but still misses `content/.agents` under default `globSync`, still needs an explicit decision on root `docs/` / `meta/` / `incidents/`, and still leaves dead listed globs unless they are deleted or prefixed.


### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-09-02T16:54:23Z)

model: claude-opus-5[1m]
role: critic

## Re-verification (ran, not cited)

Detached checkout at `16e995470c73c9449d6ee137162912db091e9de6`. `node_modules` is absent in this worktree, so I could not invoke the built extractor; I recomputed the module→file mapping over `git ls-files` with a matcher emulating `globSync` semantics, and read the shipped matcher (`packages/core/src/codebase/default-extractor.ts:182-217`) to check the emulation. Both audit anchors in the issue reproduce exactly:

- `framework-content` matches **87** files; **298** tracked `.md` files live under `content/`.
- `content-packs` matches **0** files; `content/packs/` has **6** tracked `.json` files (and **0** `.md`).

Three facts the audit did not record, and which change what the remedy has to be:

- **24 of `framework-content`'s 34 `pathGlobs` match zero files.** The module total is nonzero anyway.
- **80 of the 87 matches come from `docs/**/*.md` (76), `meta/**/*.md` (3), `incidents/**/*.md` (1)** — the three *root* trees.
- **457 tracked files are unowned by any module**, 331 of them under `content/`.

I also read the validator (`packages/core/src/verify-source/code-structure-validate.ts`), the C1 flatten (`cmd/deft-install/upgrade.go:555-575`, `upgrade_test.go:158-205`), the Content Manifest (`content/conventions/content-manifest.json`), and the `task check` wiring (`Taskfile.yml:427,467-468,471-480`).

## Findings

### 1. `blocks-the-design` — the zero-match check would not have fired on the module this issue is about

**Evidence.** `framework-content` matches 87 > 0 while 24 of its 34 globs match zero (`coding/**/*.md`, `skills/**/*.md`, `contracts/**/*.md`, `templates/**/*.md`, `core/**/*.md`, …). AC4's failure condition is per-*module* nonempty; only `content-packs` (0 total) trips it.

**Failure mode.** After the repair lands, the next relocation — a `content/skills/` → `content/guidance/` move, exactly the shape of #1875 — zeroes one glob inside a module that still matches hundreds. Module nonzero, validation green, MAP under-reports the moved subtree. That is bit-for-bit the state #4088 documents, and the guard the issue buys does not detect it.

**Disposition consequence.** The failure condition has to be **per-glob** (an unmatched glob in a required module fails), which is also what makes AC5's "diagnostics name … unmatched globs" actionable instead of decorative — as written AC5 requires the gate to *know* the unmatched globs and AC4 forbids it from *acting* on them. Two consequences follow: (a) the exception in AC4 must then be per-glob, not per-module; (b) `content/packs/**/*.md` will be permanently empty (0 `.md` under `content/packs`) and `core/**/*.md` is a ghost stem with no counterpart at the root or under `content/` — so per-glob strictness needs the exception on day one, not as a follow-up. The lean cannot bind with a module-level condition: it certifies a guard that provably does not cover its own evidence.

### 2. `blocks-the-design` — `framework-content` mis-attributes repo-dev material, so a purely additive fix makes the module worse

**Evidence.** `framework-content`'s only nonzero *directory* globs are `docs/**/*.md`, `meta/**/*.md`, `incidents/**/*.md` — 80 of its 87 matches. `content/conventions/content-manifest.json` classifies root `docs`, `meta`, and `incidents` as **`repo-dev`** ("maintainer/repo docs (FILES.md, RELEASING.md, analysis/, audits …)", "never ships", "ideas.md, suggestions.md, lessons.md, policy-changes.log"), and its `straddlePolicy` records that #1875 *split* those trees so the shippable half moved under `content/` and the maintainer-only half stayed at the root.

**Failure mode.** The issue's Why names only under-reporting. If AC1 is satisfied additively — keep the existing globs, add `content/**` — the module becomes ~418 files unioning two buckets the manifest says must not be conflated, and every MAP consumer reading "Framework Content: agent-consumed standards, strategies, skills, templates, and documentation" gets `docs/RELEASING.md` and incident postmortems presented as agent guidance. Today that module is ~92% repo-dev by count; the additive fix leaves the positive error in place and hides it behind a bigger denominator.

**Disposition consequence.** AC1 must split into two obligations — *add* the `content/` guidance stems and *re-home or drop* the root `docs`/`meta`/`incidents` globs — and AC3 needs to name the root-vs-`content/` bucket boundary explicitly rather than "matches the corrected boundaries." Note the same conflation is authored one field away, in the Architecture narrative at `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json:12` ("(1) Framework content: … standards, skills, strategies, templates, **docs, conventions**"), which AC3's "module ownership and purpose text" does not reach; leaving it makes the record self-contradictory after the fix.

### 3. `blocks-the-design` — the fail-closed check has a documented silent-pass invocation

**Evidence.** `validateCodeStructure(record, source, projectRoot = null)` (`code-structure-validate.ts:608`) is filesystem-blind for globs; `projectRoot` is used only for projection banners and glossary URIs. `validateFile` receives `projectRoot: explicitPaths ? null : root, allowStandalone: explicitPaths` (`:846-847`), and the CLI accepts positional paths (`packages/cli/src/dispatch.ts:2858-2874`) which `tasks/codebase.yml:7-18` forwards via `CLI_ARGS`.

**Failure mode.** `task codebase:validate-structure -- xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` runs with `projectRoot === null`. Any glob-matching check hung off `projectRoot` silently no-ops and prints `OK:`. An agent verifying this very fix with an explicit path — the natural way to check one file — gets a green that means nothing. A fail-closed gate with a documented bypass is not fail-closed.

**Disposition consequence.** AC4 must state the behaviour when the project root is unknown (error, skip, or `CS-CONFIG`), and either thread the root through the explicit-path form or refuse the check there loudly. `allowStandalone` exists precisely because an explicit path may not sit in a project tree, so "fails validation" is underspecified until that case is named.

### 4. `sharpens-framing` — the Content Manifest already owns this fact, fail-closed, and nothing ties the two

**Evidence.** `content/conventions/content-manifest.json` (v2, 36 `content`-bucket entries) is self-described as the "structural source of truth classifying repository entries into one of four buckets and enforcing the post-move LOCATION INVARIANT," and `verify:content-manifest` (`Taskfile.yml:427`, in `check:framework-source`) fails when a git-tracked `content/` child has no manifest entry. Its content bucket enumerates exactly the stems this repair needs, including the four `framework-content` has no stem for at all: `content/ci-cd`, `content/doctor`, `content/secrets`, `content/vbrief` (plus `content/.agents` and `content/packs`).

**Failure mode.** Hand-repairing the glob list creates a third hand-maintained copy of a classification two gates already own. The next content move updates the manifest (a gate forces it) and leaves `codeStructure` stale (nothing forces it) — and per finding 1 the new zero-match check will not notice, because the module stays nonzero. This is the same drift class, one issue later.

**Disposition consequence.** Add a criterion tying the two — derive the `framework-content` stems from the manifest's content bucket, or add a manifest↔`codeStructure` drift check — and enumerate the added stems against the manifest rather than mechanically prefixing `content/` (prefixing leaves 4-5 subtrees unowned and keeps `core/**/*.md` permanently empty). This sharpens rather than blocks because the manifest gate is deliberately framework-source-only (`Taskfile.yml:420-427` targets `DEFT_ROOT`, "a consumer install has no `content/` + `engine/` top-level split to audit"), so any tie can only be a repo-local gate; the consumer-facing half of the remedy still has to stand on findings 1 and 3.

### 5. `sharpens-framing` — "matches" has two incompatible definitions in the code the check will live next to

**Evidence.** `curatedModules` computes `globFiles` per module and reports `fileCount` from that (`default-extractor.ts:292-312`), while `fileToModule` assigns each path to the **first declaring module** (`:295-299`). A module can have a nonzero `fileCount` and own zero files.

**Failure mode.** Concretely, if the repair gives `framework-content` a broad `content/**/*.md` and it is declared first (it is, at `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json:28`), every markdown file under `content/packs/` attributes to `framework-content` while `content-packs` still passes AC2 through its `.json` glob. `CS-GLOB-CONFLICT` will not see it: that check compares glob **strings** for equality (`code-structure-validate.ts` `validateModule`), so overlapping-but-unequal globs are invisible.

**Disposition consequence.** AC4 must say which notion of "matches" the gate uses (per-module glob hits, or post-`fileToModule` ownership), and the repair should prefer disjoint stems over a broad `content/**` so declaration order carries no meaning.

### 6. `sharpens-framing` — the gate's file universe is the working tree, unlike the repo's existing structural gate

**Evidence.** `globFiles` uses `globSync` over the working tree (`default-extractor.ts:180-217`), skipping only `SKIP_DIRS`. `verify:content-manifest` deliberately uses `git ls-files` — "Uses `git ls-files content` (tracked truth), so untracked caches are excluded" (`packages/core/src/verify-source/content-manifest.ts:218-232`).

**Failure mode.** A fail-closed check wired into `task check` (`Taskfile.yml:467`) whose verdict depends on untracked local state is non-hermetic: the same commit passes in one worktree and fails in a sparse or partial checkout, and an untracked scratch file can satisfy a glob that has no tracked members. Since this repo runs `task check` from swarm worktrees, that is a live divergence, not a theoretical one.

**Disposition consequence.** Name the file universe in AC4 and prefer tracked truth, matching the precedent the sibling structural gate already set.

### 7. `sharpens-framing` — rollout: the repo has an advisory-then-enforce idiom and AC4 skips it, on a consumer-facing task

**Evidence.** `codebase:validate-structure` runs `dir: '{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}'` (`tasks/codebase.yml:9`) and `discoverCodeStructurePaths` resolves the *consumer's* PROJECT-DEFINITION plus every lifecycle artifact carrying a `codeStructure` record. The house pattern for new fail-closed structural checks is fail-open by default with an `--enforce` shim wired only into `check:framework-source` (`verify-contained-writes-enforce`, `Taskfile.yml:471,477-486`), mirrored by `verify:judgment-gates --enforce` staying opt-in. Also `NFR-4` (`xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json:16`) states `codeStructure` "must contain authored **intent** only, not derived facts such as … file counts" — a record whose declared purpose is intent legitimately describes structure ahead of the files.

**Failure mode.** A consumer who declares a module before writing the code — sanctioned by NFR-4 — hard-fails `task check` with no phase-in and no discoverable remedy until they learn an `allowEmpty`-style field exists. Blast radius here is every install, not this repo.

**Disposition consequence.** Add a criterion for the rollout shape: three-state exit, default advisory, `--enforce` in `check:framework-source`, and an explicit statement of whether the check is framework-source-only or consumer-facing.

### 8. `sharpens-framing` — `allowEmpty` as specified is an unjustified self-service opt-out

**Evidence.** AC4's exception carries no required rationale, owner, or expiry. The same record's `pathOwnership` entries do carry one (`xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json:152,158`: `"rationale": "Canonical codeStructure intent lives only at …"`).

**Failure mode.** The whole value delivered here is that `content-packs` was *visibly* zero for long enough to be audited. The next agent that hits this gate red adds `allowEmpty: true` and the module goes dark permanently — with no artifact saying why, and nothing to review later. This is the standard fail-closed-with-authored-escape-hatch collapse, and it is one line from happening.

**Disposition consequence.** AC4 should require the exception to carry a non-empty rationale (and ideally the issue that sanctioned it), matching `pathOwnership`'s existing shape, and the validator should reject a bare boolean.

## Steelman, road-not-taken, and what would flip me

I chose among three mechanisms: per-glob unmatched detection (finding 1), deriving the stems from the Content Manifest (finding 4), and a whole-tree ownership-completeness check over the 457 unowned files. **I rejected the completeness check** as the primary remedy: `codeStructure` is authored intent with a bounded module count (`validateBoundedness` warns when `pathOwnership` grows past `max(12, modules*3)`), so a coverage gate would push the record toward the per-file registry that check exists to prevent, and `history/` (46 unowned) plus `docs-site/` are legitimately unowned.

**Strongest rejected position, stated fairly:** the recorded lean is defensible precisely *because* the zero-match check is the cheap, mechanical, layout-independent half. Per-glob strictness fails legitimately-aspirational globs (NFR-4 says intent, and `content/packs/**/*.md` is a live example of a glob that is not wrong merely because it is empty); welding `codeStructure` to `content-manifest.json` couples authored intent to a framework-source-only gate a consumer does not have. On that reading, module-level is the right granularity and my finding 1 is over-engineering.

**What would flip me:** if the empty-module check were declared framework-source-only diagnostics rather than a consumer-facing gate, findings 6 and 7 collapse to footnotes and 4 weakens to "second copy, but gated." **What survives either way:** findings 1, 2, and 3. Finding 1 because the guard's stated purpose is preventing recurrence of the evidence in the Why and it demonstrably does not cover it — the per-glob exception the steelman demands is an argument for pairing per-glob strictness with a per-glob exception, not for staying at module granularity. Finding 2 because the mis-attribution is a positive error the ACs never remove. Finding 3 because a fail-closed claim with a documented green bypass is not a fail-closed claim.

## Injection / swarm lens

Fires: the target changes a check wired into `task check` and an authored record that ships through the C1 flatten to consumer installs. Traced and found clean — `globFiles` walks from `realpathSync(resolve(projectRoot))`, `safeRelativePath` already refuses absolute paths, `~`, `$`, backslashes and `..` in every glob, and the record is repo-tracked, so no untrusted path reaches the walk. The one authority change the design does introduce is the `allowEmpty` opt-out (finding 8): a new authored field that disables a gate, with no required justification — that is the injection-relevant surface here, and it is a data-plane self-grant rather than an input-parsing bug. No cross-worktree hazard is added: `.planning/codebase/MAP.md` is absent/gitignored and `checkCodebaseMapFresh` returns clean when the projection does not exist (`map-fresh.ts:22-29`), which #1932 settled deliberately to avoid mechanical MAP collisions across concurrent branches. Finding 6 (working-tree file universe) is the worktree-shaped risk and is filed there rather than here.

## Footnotes

- `footnote` — The dispatch reason says the contract "gates MAP truth." `.planning/codebase/MAP.md` is not present in the tree, and `checkCodebaseMapFresh` returns no findings when the projection is absent (`map-fresh.ts:22-29`), so MAP truth is advisory-on-demand, not a committed gated artifact. This does not change the spend (N≥3 is permission, and blast radius holds via `task check` and consumer installs) and carries no disposition weight — but the framing should not claim a gate that no-ops on a clean checkout.
- `footnote` — `contentHashPaths` is seeded from `fileToModule.keys()` (`default-extractor.ts:713-717`), i.e. only files that already match a module glob. Today the 331 unowned tracked files under `content/` are outside the MAP's own content hash, so the freshness signal is blind to them. The repair incidentally shrinks this, which is worth knowing but is not a separate obligation.
- `footnote` — AC6 ("reviewed module counts are covered by focused tests"): counts are a function of the tree, so a test asserting `87` or `298` is a date-stamped fixture that churns on the next content addition. Property assertions (every declared glob matches ≥1 tracked file; no module spans two manifest buckets) are the durable form.

## Verdict

The evidence is real, and the data correction is necessary, but the recorded lean does not close the failure class as written. At dispatch SHA `16e995470c73c9449d6ee137162912db091e9de6`, `task codebase:validate-structure -- --json` is green; the default extractor reports `framework-content=87` and `content-packs=0`; the tree contains 298 Markdown files below `content/` and six JSON pack files below `content/packs/`. ## Existing mechanism inventory

- `validateCodeStructure` validates module shape and path syntax but never resolves files (`packages/core/src/verify-source/code-structure-validate.ts:218-277,608-639`).
- The only repository matcher is the private `globFiles` path in the default extractor. It applies `globSync`, file-only filtering, and `SKIP_DIRS`, then `curatedModules` derives counts (`packages/core/src/codebase/default-extractor.ts:182-209,264-320`).
- Direct MAP generation selects/builds an artifact and renders it without calling the structure validator (`packages/core/src/codebase/map.ts:284-315`; `packages/core/src/codebase/provider.ts:687-712`).

That separation matters to both findings below.

## blocks-the-design — Whole-module nonempty does not detect partial boundary loss

**Evidence.** `framework-content` currently has 34 globs, 24 of which match zero filtered files, but its union still contains 87 files. That is the exact under-reporting this issue is meant to prevent: all 298 `content/**/*.md` files are absent while unrelated root/docs matches keep the module nonempty. `ci-release-automation` supplies a second shape: `.github/**/*.yaml` is empty while its sibling globs make the module count 11.

**Failure mode.** A rule that fails only when a module's union is zero catches `content-packs` today but cannot catch a mistyped, moved, or partially stale glob whenever another glob still hits. After the one-time data repair, the same class can recur with green validation. A module-level `allowEmpty` also has the wrong granularity for a deliberately optional glob: enabling it would waive the entire module.

**Disposition consequence.** The design cannot bind on module-union cardinality alone. Define the invariant at the declared boundary: each required `pathGlob` must resolve at least one file under the extractor's filtered semantics, with an exact, typed exception scoped to the specific optional glob (or replace multi-glob intent with a coarser boundary and test membership explicitly). Add the discriminating fixture: one module with one matching glob and one stale glob must fail, naming both module and stale glob.

## blocks-the-design — The proposed gate is not on the MAP consumer path

**Evidence.** `codebase-map --stdout` currently exits 0 and renders `content-packs | ... | 0`. The call path `writeCodebaseMap` / stdout mode -> `selectCodebaseMap` -> fallback -> `buildCodebaseMap` never invokes `validateCodeStructure`. `verify:codebase-map-fresh` is intentionally green when the projection is absent (`packages/core/src/codebase/map-fresh.ts:22-30`). The issue's current criteria allow an implementation that changes only `codebase:validate-structure` while MAP generation continues to emit a zero-file required module.

**Failure mode.** The validator and extractor can also disagree if the new check independently calls a generic globber: validation may count dependency, build, or agent-worktree files that `SKIP_DIRS` removes, while the MAP still reports zero. Explicit `--path` validation currently drops `projectRoot` in `evaluateCodeStructure` (`packages/core/src/verify-source/code-structure-validate.ts:817-848`), creating another bypass unless filesystem-check semantics are stated.

**Disposition consequence.** Require one shared module-file resolver for validation and extraction, including the same exclusion policy, and put the fail-closed result on default extraction/MAP generation as well as the standalone validator. A fixture should prove that the validator and `codebase-map --stdout` give the same nonzero/empty verdict, including an excluded-directory case and the explicit-path CLI surface. If MAP generation is intentionally allowed to render invalid authored structure, narrow the issue's MAP-truth claim and make the mandatory preflight dependency explicit instead.

## sharpens-framing — Test stable boundaries, not a volatile repository total

**Evidence.** Module `fileCount` is derived from the live tree, while displayed file lists truncate at 100 and freshness already hashes matched module files (`packages/core/src/codebase/default-extractor.ts:25,80-108,299-317`). Exact dogfood totals will change whenever valid guidance or pack files are added.

**Failure mode.** A hard-coded `298`/`6` repository test creates routine update churn; a mere `>0` assertion misses the partial-loss defect above.

**Disposition consequence.** Keep the measured totals as review evidence, but make focused fixtures assert boundary membership, zero/partial-zero behavior, exception typing, diagnostics, and validator/extractor parity. For the dogfood tree, assert that the intended `content/**/*.md` and `content/packs/**/*.json` sets are covered rather than freezing their current cardinalities.

## footnote — Authority and worktree lens

No instruction-shaped payload appeared in the in-envelope issue material. The relevant authority/shared-state concern is filesystem selection: the authored `codeStructure` drives a generated orientation artifact across local and agent worktrees. Reusing the extractor's `NON_PRODUCT_DIRS`/`SKIP_DIRS` policy prevents dependency trees and agent scratch checkouts from satisfying the new invariant. No prompt, identity, or concurrency mechanism otherwise changes here.

## Road not taken

The strongest case for exact repository count snapshots is that they would catch today's 87/0 drift with very little implementation work. I would choose that route only if module membership is intended to be a manually approved closed set. The existing contract makes counts derived from globs, so boundary and parity tests preserve the intended abstraction without making every legitimate file addition an architecture-contract edit.
